notes: HVS8, HVS9, and HVS10 are reported here as the three new unbound HVSs; HVS1, HVS2, HVS3, HVS4, HVS5, HVS6, and HVS7 are prior HVS discoveries included in this paper, with HVS1-HVS3 listed in Table 1 but excluded from the survey analyses (T:p4-b4). Catalog-name forms for the new stars differ between text and table: HVS8 is SDSS J094214.04+200322.07 in T:p3-b12 and SDSS J094214.04+200322.1 in T:p4-b0; HVS9 is SDSS J102137.08-005234.77 in T:p3-b12 and SDSS J102137.08-005234.8 in T:p4-b0; HVS10 is SDSS J120337.86+180250.35 in T:p4-b1 and SDSS J120337.85+180250.4 in T:p4-b0; both supported forms are retained. I excluded the 19 stars with 275 < v_rf < 400 km/s because the authors explicitly call them only possibly bound HVSs and use only the well-defined unbound sample (T:p3-b9). I also excluded SDSS J144955.58+310351.4, which is called a possibly bound HVS and not retained as unbound in the final sample (T:p7-b2).

HVS2: Target HVS2 = US 708. Table 1 gives Galactocentric radius R_GC = 26 kpc (not a heliocentric distance), heliocentric radial velocity v_⊙ = 708 km/s, and v_rf = 717 km/s. The table caption (T:p4-b4) states v_rf is a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity and not a full space velocity; accordingly it is recorded as a lower bound on the galactocentric rest-frame speed. No right ascension, declination, parallax, heliocentric distance, proper motions, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star in the supplied material. Table 1 also notes HVS2 is included but excluded from the survey analyses (T:p4-b4: "We include HVS1, HVS2, and HVS3 in Table 1 but exclude them from our analyses").

HVS3: Target is HVS3 (= HE 0437-5439), row 3 of Table 1 (T:p4-b0 / I:p4-b0). The paper does not report equatorial coordinates (ra, dec), heliocentric distance, parallax, or proper motions for this star; it lists only Galactic coordinates (l = 263.04 deg, b = -40.91 deg), so those quantities are omitted. The Galactocentric radius R_GC = 62 kpc in Table 1 is not a heliocentric distance. The v_rf value of 548 km/s is explicitly described as a minimum rest-frame velocity (not a full space velocity), because proper motions are unknown (T:p4-b6). Table 1 reports no formal errors; the text notes heliocentric radial velocities are accurate to ±11 km/s (T:p4-b6). HVS3 is included in Table 1 but excluded from the paper's analyses (T:p4-b4); no bound/unbound probability is given specifically for it.

HVS4: HVS4 is identified as SDSS J091301.01+305119.8. Table 1 (T:p4-b0, I:p4-b0) gives its Galactocentric radius, heliocentric radial velocity, minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, and catalog designation, but no individual uncertainties. The text at T:p4-b4 defines the columns and explicitly states that v_rf is a minimum rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity; T:p4-b6 gives the general ±11 km/s B-type-star radial-velocity accuracy. The J2000 RA/Dec are taken from the SDSS designation. No heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS4.

HVS5: At T:p4-b0, the HVS5 row lists v_⊙ = 551 km/s and v_rf = 647 km/s. At T:p4-b4, the authors define v_⊙ as heliocentric radial velocity and v_rf as the minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, explicitly not a full space velocity; I therefore retain v_rf only as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. The R_GC = 45 kpc value is a Galactocentric radius, not a heliocentric distance. The RA and Dec are parsed from the SDSS J2000 catalog designation in the Table 1 Catalog column, because no separate HVS5 coordinate columns are given. No HVS5-specific distance, parallax, proper motions, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported.

HVS6: Target star: HVS6 = SDSS J110557.45+093439.5 (Table 1 row hvs6). Table 1 reports no uncertainties for any entry; §3.1/Table 1 note states that formal uncertainties are misleadingly small compared to unknown systematics (heliocentric velocities accurate to ±11 km/s, but the proper-motion contribution to v_rf is unconstrained). The v_rf value is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity derived from the radial component only, so it is a lower limit to the total space velocity rather than a full three-dimensional speed. No heliocentric distance, parallax, or proper motions are reported for HVS6; the survey magnitude limits (15 < g'_0 < 19.5; heliocentric 12 < d < 100 kpc for 3 Msun stars) are sample selection ranges, not individual values. RA and Dec are not tabulated separately; they are taken from the SDSS J2000 sexagesimal designation given as the catalog identification in Table 1. No individual bound/unbound probability is quantified for HVS6.

HVS7: Table 1 reports no formal uncertainties for HVS7. Its v_rf=421 km/s is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame line-of-sight velocity, not a full 3D space velocity. The paper does not report HVS7 equatorial coordinates as a separate measurement, nor parallax, proper motion, heliocentric distance, or bound probability.

HVS8: Table 1 (T:p4-b0) gives HVS8 v_⊙ = 511 km s^-1 and v_rf = 429 km s^-1, whereas §3.1 (T:p4-b1) gives +512 ± 10 km s^-1 heliocentric and a minimum +430 km s^-1; both are recorded. The table's v_rf is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity and not a full space velocity, so these are treated as lower bounds. The catalog identifier is SDSS J094214.04+200322.07 in §3.1 (T:p3-b12) and SDSS J094214.04+200322.1 in Table 1; RA/Dec were parsed from these J2000 identifiers. The paper describes HVS8 as "very likely unbound" but gives no numerical bound/unbound probability.

HVS9: At T:p4-b0 (Table 1) and T:p4-b2 (§3.1), HVS9 has slightly different reported velocities: Table 1 gives v⊙ = 628 km/s and v_rf = 485 km/s, while §3.1 gives +632 ± 11 km/s heliocentric and a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity of +489 km/s. Table 1 states its velocities are weighted averages of multiple observations; both table and §3.1 values are retained. The paper's v_rf is explicitly a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity, so it is recorded as a lower limit on the total speed. No explicit heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motions, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for HVS9; the text only states that it is "certainly unbound." The catalog designation is printed as SDSS J102137.08-005234.8 in Table 1 and SDSS J102137.08-005234.77 at T:p3-b12; RA/Dec are not presented as separate tabulated quantities.

HVS1: Target HVS1 is SDSS J090744.99+024506.9 (Table 1). No explicit right ascension or declination is tabulated for HVS1; coordinates are only encoded in the catalog name. Table 1 states that velocities changed slightly from previous work and gives the weighted average of multiple observations (840 km/s heliocentric); the individual HVS1 measurements in §3.2 are 853±12, 816±14, and 832±13 km/s, and HVS1 may be a slowly pulsating B variable. The paper notes that v_rf is a minimum rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity; the earlier value of at least +709±12 km/s (Brown et al. 2005) is also reported. HVS1 is included in Table 1 but excluded from the survey analyses.

HVS10: Table 1 has no formal errors; +/-10 km/s is from section 3.1. v_rf is a minimum, not full space velocity, so it is a lower bound. No heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motion, or bound probability is explicitly given for HVS10. The two SDSS designations differ slightly due to rounding.
